ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The attached diagram shows a square containing two circles. The larger circle is in the bottom-left part of the square and is tangent to the left and bottom sides. The smaller circle is in the top-right part of the square and is tangent to the top and right sides. The two circles touch each other, and their centers lie along the same bottom-left to top-right diagonal of the square. Reasoning: Let the square be the unit square with bottom-left corner (0,0) and top-right corner (1,1). Let the radius of the larger circle be R, so its center is (R,R). Let the radius of the smaller circle be r, so its center is (1-r,1-r). Since the two circles touch, the distance between their centers equals R+r. The horizontal and vertical separations between the centers are both 1-r-R, so the center distance is sqrt((1-r-R)^2+(1-r-R)^2)=sqrt(2)(1-R-r). Let s=R+r. Then sqrt(2)(1-s)=s. Solving gives sqrt(2)=s(1+sqrt(2)), so s=sqrt(2)/(1+sqrt(2))=2-sqrt(2). Therefore, the sum of the radii is 2-sqrt(2) cm.
